Assume all transactions are attempting to access the same database resource. 
Transaction Operation Requested Lock Type Requested 
T1 Read Shared (S-lock) 
T2 Read Shared (S-lock) 
T3 Write Exclusive (X-lock) 
T4 Read Shared (S-lock) 
Based on standard DBMS lock compatibility rules, which of the following statements is correct?
options: Transactions T1, T2, and T4 can simultaneously hold S-locks on the same resource.
Transaction T3 can obtain an X-lock while T1 holds an S-lock.
Transaction T4 can read the resource while T3 holds an X-lock.
An S-lock and an X-lock are compatible on the same resource.

questions.answer: Transactions T1, T2, and T4 can simultaneously hold S-locks on the same resource.

Which of the following scenarios can lead to starvation in process scheduling?
options: A process is stuck in a circular wait due to resource allocation.
A high-priority process continuously preempts a lower-priority process.
All processes have equal priority and resources are allocated fairly.
Processes are executed in the order of their arrival without preemption.
Processes communicate with each other to avoid mutual exclusion violations.
questions.answer: A high-priority process continuously preempts a lower-priority process.

options:
A table is in 3NF if it is in 2NF and every non-prime attribute is non-transitively dependent on every key 
of the table.

A table is in 3NF if it is in 2NF and every non -prime attribute is dependent on every non-key attribute 
of the table.

A table is in 3NF if it has no transitive dependencies and every non -prime attribute is partially 
dependent on a candidate key.

of the table.
